title: Supabase Project & Database
description: Manage Supabase projects, run SQL, inspect tables, generate types, and deploy edge functions via the official Supabase MCP server.

env_vars.name: SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN
env_vars.description: Supabase personal access token. Create one at supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens; authenticates the server to the Management API. Pass via env, never inline in args (doctrine #6).

auth.recipe: create a personal access token at supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens, then set SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN; scope the server to one project with `--project-ref` and prefer `--read-only`.

sample_tools.name: list_projects
sample_tools.summary: List all Supabase projects for the user (account-scoped).

sample_tools.name: list_tables
sample_tools.summary: List all tables within the specified schemas.

sample_tools.name: execute_sql
sample_tools.summary: Execute raw SQL against the database (runs as a read-only Postgres user in read-only mode).

sample_tools.name: search_docs
sample_tools.summary: Search the Supabase documentation for up-to-date guidance.

sample_tools.name: get_logs
sample_tools.summary: Get logs for a project by service type (api, postgres, auth, storage, …).

sample_tools.name: generate_typescript_types
sample_tools.summary: Generate TypeScript types from the database schema.

sample_tools.name: list_edge_functions
sample_tools.summary: List all Edge Functions in a project.

known_limitations: Requires a Supabase personal access token (SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN); without it the server cannot authenticate to the Management API and tools return an auth error.
Without `--project-ref` the server can access every project in your Supabase account; scope it to a single project (account-level tools like list_projects are then disabled).

Mutating tools (apply_migration, create_project, deploy_edge_function, branch operations) act on real infrastructure — Supabase recommends `--read-only` and a non-production project; read-only mode runs execute_sql as a read-only Postgres user and disables mutating tools.
Destructive-action audit (X2.18): delete_branch is flagged in `destructive_tools` and is blocked when the trust policy sets `allowDestructive: false`.

client_install.claude_desktop: Add to claude_desktop_config.json mcpServers as `supabase`: { command: npx, args: [-y, @supabase/mcp-server-supabase, --read-only, --project-ref=<ref>], env: { SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN: "sbp_..." } }.
client_install.cursor: Settings → MCP → Add: name `supabase`, command `npx -y @supabase/mcp-server-supabase --read-only --project-ref=<ref>`; set SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN in the env.
client_install.vscode: Add to .vscode/mcp.json servers as `supabase` (VS Code Insider, MCP preview); supply SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN via inputs.
